concern: Enhanced binding or covalent warhead modification
system_prompt: You are an expert computational medicinal chemist. Always respond with valid JSON containing a 'modifications' list. Each modification must include 'description', 'smiles', and 'rationale' fields.

modifications.description: Add a hydroxymethyl group to the nitrile-bearing cyclopropyl ring to enhance hydrogen bonding with the catalytic dyad.
modifications.rationale: The hydroxymethyl group may form additional hydrogen bonds with the catalytic residues of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro, potentially improving binding potency.

modifications.description: Replace one trifluoromethyl group with a difluoromethyl group to reduce steric hindrance while maintaining strong hydrophobic interactions.
modifications.rationale: Reducing the bulkiness of the trifluoromethyl group could improve fit within the binding pocket, enhancing selectivity and potency.

modifications.description: Incorporate a methoxyl group at the amide nitrogen to improve hydrogen bonding interactions with adjacent residues.
modifications.rationale: The methoxyl group may act as both a hydrogen bond donor and acceptor, enhancing interactions with the protease active site.

modifications.description: Add a fluorine atom to the cyclopropyl ring to increase hydrophobic interactions with the nonpolar region of the binding pocket.
modifications.rationale: Fluorination of the cyclopropyl ring can increase binding affinity by enhancing hydrophobic interactions and electronic effects.

modifications.description: Introduce a phenyl group to the terminal nitrile for π-π stacking interactions with aromatic residues in the binding site.
modifications.rationale: The phenyl group can engage in π-π stacking or hydrophobic interactions, potentially improving binding affinity and selectivity.
